Job Purpose:
Orchestrate the end-to-end Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy and operational delivery for the entire Digital Content Partnership ecosystem. As a critical leadership role, this position bridges commercial strategy and technical execution by governing partner integrations, managing digital service operations, and driving targeted campaign cadences to accelerate time-to-market and aggressively boost the penetration rate of digital lifestyle and financial services.

Main Responsibility:
Strategic Go-To-Market (GTM) Leadership: Define and direct the overarching GTM strategy for all digital partnership initiatives. Align product roadmaps, target segmentation, and launch timelines across various commercial pillars (Gaming, OTT, Financial Services) to ensure cohesive and impactful market entry.
End-to-End Partner Integration & Delivery: Oversee the technical and commercial onboarding of new partners. Lead cross-functional squads (spanning IT, Billing, Network, and external partner engineering teams) to ensure complex API integrations, user journeys, and billing mechanisms are delivered seamlessly, on time, and within budget.
Digital Service Operations & Incident Governance: Command the day-to-day operational health of all live digital services. Establish robust monitoring frameworks, govern SLA adherence, and lead rapid-response troubleshooting to resolve service outages, integration bottlenecks, or customer journey friction.
Campaign Orchestration & Penetration Growth: Direct the scheduling, execution, and lifecycle management of promotional campaigns designed to drive digital service adoption. Optimize the promotional calendar to maximize user penetration, ensuring campaigns hit targeted growth metrics without oversaturating the subscriber base.
Performance Reporting & Continuous Optimization: Establish comprehensive reporting mechanisms and operational dashboards for senior executive visibility. Translate complex delivery metrics and campaign performance data into actionable insights to refine future GTM frameworks and improve overall operational efficiency.

Key Output:

Accelerated Time-to-Market (TTM): A measurable, systemic reduction in the lead time from commercial contract signature to live commercial launch, driven by standardized, highly efficient delivery workflows.

Maximized Digital Service Penetration: A defined, continuous increase in the adoption and active penetration rates of digital partnership services, directly resulting from well-scheduled, high-impact GTM campaigns.

Operational Excellence & High Service Uptime: Achievement of stringent operational SLAs characterized by high transaction success rates, minimal digital service downtime, and the rapid, permanent resolution of technical incidents.

Unified Delivery Architecture: The successful implementation of a scalable, repeatable GTM and operational framework that eliminates internal silos and standardizes how the telco integrates and launches third-party digital services.

su-isat-59140844.d:
The Head of Customer Acquisition & Fulfillment owns the end-to-end journey of a sold order into an active FTTH service — from customer verification and validation through to installation, activation, and service delivery. This is an AVP-level role leading two functions, Verification & Validation and Service Delivery, and is accountable for ensuring genuine customer acquisition, preventing fraud/recycle-customer cases, and delivering the installation and activation experience promised at the point of sale. Beyond the order itself, the role orchestrates the full onboarding ecosystem — Sales, digital ordering channels, verification, field technicians, and fiber partners — so that acquisition volume grows without compromising quality, and it remains accountable for service quality in the customer's early life after activation. The role plays a critical part in protecting revenue integrity and driving FTTH's targets for interaction volume, First Call Resolution (FCR), and Customer Care CSAT, by ensuring orders are fulfilled right the first time and customers become genuine, satisfied, and retained subscribers.

Scope of Work

Area of Responsibilities

Key Activities

Deliverables

1. Customer Acquisition (Verification & Validation)

- Lead the Verification & Validation team to confirm FTTH service availability at the customer's location against coverage maps/databases and required infrastructure.

- Ensure every prospective customer is validated as a genuine customer prior to onboarding, preventing recycle-customer / fraud cases.

- Set, monitor, and continuously improve verification SLA and accuracy targets; escalate coverage or infrastructure gaps to Technology/Network partners.

Verification & Validation SOP and coverage / infrastructure check workflow

Verification SLA and accuracy performance dashboard

Fraud / recycle-customer detection and escalation log.

2. Order Fulfillment & Service Delivery

- Lead the Service Delivery function across order management, installation scheduling, site preparation, installation/activation, and quality assurance (interim coverage while the dedicated Head of Service Delivery role is vacant).

- Ensure customer orders progress smoothly from sale through activation, coordinating with Sales, Billing, Technical, and Field Partner teams.

- Own installation SLA performance, activation turnaround time, and first-time-right installation quality.

Order-to-activation SOP covering scheduling, site prep, installation, and activation;

installation SLA and activation turnaround time report;

first-time-right installation quality scorecard.

3. End-to-End Order-to-Activation Ownership

- Act as the single point of accountability for the full journey from sold order to a genuine, verified, and successfully installed/activated service.

- Build and maintain an integrated reporting cadence covering verification accuracy, installation SLA, activation success rate, and CSAT.

- Resolve cross-functional bottlenecks between the acquisition (verification) and fulfillment (installation/activation) stages.

integrated acquisition-to-fulfillment performance dashboard (verification accuracy, installation SLA, activation success rate, CSAT)

cross-functional bottleneck/issue log with resolution status

monthly end-to-end funnel report (sold order → verified → installed → activated).

4. Recycle-Customer Prevention & Verification Integrity

- Design and own a risk-based verification framework (identity/NIK, address, payment and bad-debt history, prior disconnection and blacklist screening) with clear auto-pass, auto-review, and manual-verification tiers, so recycle and fraudulent customers are blocked before order confirmation while genuine customers stay on a fast, low-friction path.

- Govern both sides of the trade-off — false-positive rate (genuine customers rejected or delayed) and false-negative rate (recycle customers admitted) — and recalibrate rules, thresholds, and blacklist criteria together with Sales, Finance/Collection, and Fraud Management.

- Own the authority to reject, hold, or release high-risk orders, and ensure every verification touchpoint follows approved script, channel, and maximum-contact standards so that tightened controls do not increase customer effort, order drop-off, or CSAT loss.

Risk-based verification & anti-recycle policy, including tiering rules, blacklist criteria, and decision authority matrix

Recycle/fraud prevention scorecard: recycle-customer rate, detection rate, false-positive rate, and verification turnaround time

Verification customer-experience standard with drop-off/CSAT tracking, and monthly rule-calibration review minutes.

5. Sales & Digital Order Journey Collaboration (Cancel-Registration Reduction)

- Partner with HBB & FWA Sales, HBB Product, and the digital application/web owners to simplify the customer ordering journey — coverage check, registration, document upload, payment, and installation scheduling — reducing steps, rework, and abandonment.

- Own the analysis of cancelled and abandoned registrations by journey stage, channel, sales agent, and region, and convert the findings into a prioritised change backlog with the application owners.

- Agree and track joint KPIs with Sales and application owners (order completion rate, cancel-registration rate, order-to-verified cycle time), including agent- and channel-level feedback on mis-sold, incomplete, or out-of-coverage orders.

Order journey funnel analysis (order → registration → payment → verified) with drop-off and cancellation root-cause breakdown

Prioritised digital ordering-journey improvement backlog agreed with product/application owners, with before-after impact tracking

Joint Sales–Fulfillment KPI dashboard and monthly Sales–Product–Fulfillment review forum minutes with action tracker.

6. End-to-End Onboarding Journey Orchestration

- Own the design and governance of the end-to-end onboarding journey so that Sales, Verification & Validation, field technicians, fiber partners (AMT, Iforte), Network/Technology, Billing, and the contact center operate as one cohesive chain with clear handover points, SLAs, and RACI.

- Chair a cross-functional onboarding governance forum to resolve interlock issues (coverage versus sale, port and material availability, technician scheduling, partner capacity) and enforce the quality gates that protect growth: verified feasibility before installation, and completed checklist plus customer confirmation before activation.

- Model verification, technician, and fiber-partner capacity against the sales forecast, flag capacity risk to Sales and Leadership early, and drive one shared onboarding scorecard so every stakeholder is measured on the same end-to-end outcome.

End-to-end onboarding journey map with RACI, handover SLAs, and quality gates across all internal and partner stakeholders

Cross-functional onboarding governance forum: cadence, minutes, escalation matrix, and issue-resolution log

Acquisition quality index (gross orders → verified → activated → early cancellation/churn) with capacity-versus-forecast risk flags.

7. Post-Onboarding Service Quality (Early-Life Customer Experience)

- Own service quality for the first 30/60/90 days after activation — early-life fault rate, repeat trouble tickets, early complaints, and early churn.

- Run a structured post-installation follow-up and onboarding CSAT/NPS programme, and feed the results back to technicians, fiber partners, and sales channels as accountable quality signals.

- Analyse early-life complaints by root cause (installation workmanship, ONT/device, network, billing, or expectation gap created at the point of sale), drive upstream corrective action with the accountable owner, and escalate systemic issues to the VP-Head of HBB Operations.

Post-onboarding service quality dashboard (D+7 / D+30 / D+90 fault rate, repeat ticket rate, early churn)
